title: What is an atoll? A reef with a lagoon inside

sources.name: NOAA — How do coral reefs form?
Toomey et al. (2016), USGS — Cenozoic sea level and the rise of modern rimmed atolls

practice: Fancy another geography discovery? Try World Capitals.

sections.html:
An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef that surrounds, or nearly surrounds, a lagoon. The lagoon is the water inside; the reef forms its boundary.

From above, an atoll can look like a necklace dropped into the sea. Some beads are sandy islands. Others are sections of reef beneath the water.
sections.title: A ring in the ocean

sections.html:
NOAA describes atolls with islands and gaps in the reef. You do not need one continuous strip of dry land to make the ring.

The classic explanation starts with coral growing around a volcanic island. As the island slowly sinks and the reef grows upwards, a lagoon separates the reef from the land. Eventually, the island can disappear below sea level.
sections.title: Not a solid hoop of land

sections.html:
That is a useful starting picture, rather than a complete recipe for every atoll. Changing sea levels, reef growth, sediment and the dissolving of carbonate rock also shape the result.

USGS research using Enewetak Atoll and computer models explores how those processes help create the raised reef rim. Nature rarely sticks to one neat sketch.
sections.title: The full story has more moving parts

sections.html:
A lagoon is a body of water partly separated from a larger one by a natural barrier. Coastal lagoons exist too, so a lagoon does not automatically mean an atoll.

For two other landscapes worth a closer look, meet a valley with the sea inside and discover where the ocean gets its salt.
sections.title: Atoll or lagoon? Look at what you mean

description: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef around a lagoon. Discover why its islands can look like a broken necklace, and why the water inside has a different name.

options: Any river flowing towards the sea
A mountain valley with no water
A ring-shaped coral reef around, or nearly around, a lagoon
questions.explanation: The atoll is the reef formation around a lagoon, not the water alone.

questions.prompt: Must an atoll be one continuous strip of dry land?
options: Yes, gaps change it into a fjord
Yes, the whole reef must be above water
No, the reef can have islands and gaps
questions.explanation: Parts of the reef may be underwater and gaps may connect the lagoon with the ocean.

questions.prompt: Which word names the water inside an atoll’s reef?
questions.explanation: The lagoon is the body of water inside. The atoll names the surrounding reef formation.
